text:
Alex W: FYI canary 12: batch-assembly saw sudden OOMs under load :warning: Repro on g4-1 with long prefix loads. Stack: batch assembler -> kv cache eviction -> OOM. Anyone seen this pattern after yesterday's kernel switch?

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-17T23:15 rolled r12345 -> kernel selection change: prefer 'matmul16_fast' for short sequences.

Marta P: I pulled traces — there's a clear spike in KV allocations during batch formation. Quick summary: +13% kv-allocs at enqueue time vs baseline. Looks like the batcher is still targeting token_budget without accounting for kv footprin ts.

Rohan S: Profiling snippet (from the canary run):
```
avg_batch_tokens=980
avg_kv_bytes_per_request=14MB
kv_cache_active=78%
gpu_free_before_batch=2.1GB
```
We're often starting batches with <2GB free which trips soft-eviction and then OOMs.

Jiayi L: Hypothesis: the new kernel reduces compute latency but increases temporary scratch or changes memory alignment so kv+scratch > headroom. Also batch formation currently uses token budget only — no kv estimate. We should make admission kv-aware.

Alex W: Proposal for quick mitigation:
1) add per-request kv_estimator (seq_len + metadata-based heuristics)
2) maintain gpu.kv_reserved and kv_headroom counters
3) admission rule: if gpu.kv_reserved + sum(req.kv_est) > gpu.kv_headroom then hold requests in a separate hold-queue rather than adding to current batch
4) when kv_pressure > threshold reduce token_budget_target (e.g., *0.75) and prefer memory-slim kernels.

Marta P: +1. Also suggest a soft-eviction probe: allow one controlled eviction attempt if a batch is stuck, but prefer admission shedding to avoid catastrophic OOM loops. And add a kernel_fallback list: when pressure high pick matmul16_mem_slim. Tradeoff: ~5-8% throughput drop but avoids OOMs.

Rohan S: Ran a short sim with kv-aware admission and token_target*0.8 under pressure: OOMs dropped to 0 in a 1h stress, p95 latency rose ~6%, tail jitter reduced because we avoided kernel restarts. Worth trying in canary.

Alex W: Quick pseudocode for the admission change:
```
// on enqueue
req.kv_est = estimate_kv(req)
if gpu.kv_reserved + req.kv_est > gpu.kv_headroom:
  req.hold = true  // push to hold-queue
else:
  add_to_batch(req)
```
Also keep a sliding window metric of recent kv_evictions_count to flip to aggressive shedding mode.

Jiayi L: I'll open a small PR: runtime/batcher/kv_admission.{cc,py} with flags: kv_headroom_ratio=0.12, hold_queue_size=256, kernel_preference_on_pressure=['matmul16_mem_slim']. Will add counters: kv_admission_rejects, kv_pressure_pct and emit per-batch kv_reserved snapshot to tracing.

deploy-bot: Created canary job kv-admission-probe on cluster canary-4. Job id j-9982. Monitor dashboard: /dashboards/eng-runtime/kv_admission.

Alex W: Great — run a 2h soak and we'll reassess. If stable, plan rollout to staging. Rollback plan: revert kernel selection + disable kv_admission flag.

Marta P: One more ask: update tracing to include kernel_choice and kv_reserved at batch start. That should make root-cause easier next time.

Alex W: Agreed. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
